openQuestions.q: CHK-002 makes review_pass_set consume core/owner-session.ts getSessionIdentity() and the story-owner-lease read path to add writer-session provenance. owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md (B-a781, status 'execution plan; documentation only') requires 'two-host review evidence over the current version of this document' before 'any future story implements runtime code from this plan' or changes owner-lease/lifecycle/host-adapter/scope-guard code, and its reviewer 'should reject code work that cites this plan without fresh two-host review evidence'. Separately, session-ownership-and-write-leases.md's own Out-of-Scope section states that design does not solve 'reviewer identity attestation'. Does CHK-002 count as implementing runtime code from the owner-session-contract plan (triggering the two-host-review precondition), or is it a downstream consumer of the already-implemented session facade (per session-ownership-and-write-leases.md's 'B-9089 implements that runtime contract') and therefore exempt? And does CHK-002's warn/enforce provenance layer overstep the stated 'reviewer identity attestation' non-goal, or is it sufficiently distinct (coordination-level deterrent, not attestation) to stay compatible? None of this story's PLAN artifacts (understanding.json, decision.json, checklist, plan.md) cite or address either document.

The implementation reviewer should reject code work that cites this plan without fresh two-host review evidence bound to the document version it implements.' session-ownership-and-write-leases.md Out of Scope: 'This design does not solve: ... reviewer identity attestation'.
sourcePointers: docs/requirements/decisions/owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md#two-host-review-evidence-before-implementation (lines 359-381: before any future story implements runtime code from this plan)
docs/requirements/decisions/session-ownership-and-write-leases.md (lines 285-291: non-goals incl. reviewer identity attestation — require a stronger trust model and should be separate work)
openQuestions.resolution: No two-host precondition is triggered and no non-goal is overstepped, with one explicit boundary. (A) owner-session-contract-execution-plan.md gates stories that implement runtime code FROM that plan (its R1-R6: shared resolver, host adapters, generated-token fallback, core env-read cleanup): CHK-002 implements none of these — plan.md marks core/owner-session.ts as read-only import; we only CALL the existing exported getSessionIdentity() API and read the existing owner lease. Boundary written into this resolution: if DEV finds it must modify owner-session.ts resolver internals, that edit is out of scope for B-3b05 until the two-host review evidence over the current document version is recorded first. (B) session-ownership-and-write-leases.md lists reviewer identity attestation as a non-goal requiring a stronger trust model; CHK-002 stays inside the lease trust model — it compares two process-local coordination ids for equality, persists sessionSource with documented forgeability, uses neutral same_session_write semantics (decision preMortem 3), and claims deterrence + audit trail, never attestation. Code/doc wording must not use the word attestation for this flag.

CHK-002 changes review_pass_set's signature domain (a REVIEW-phase gate/process-fact artifact). But the actually-implemented mechanism per story-lifecycle.md and three-round-two-host-review-escalation-execution-plan.md triggers 3x2 only when 'the first lifecycle REVIEW round records at least two countable reviewer problems' -- a finding-count threshold, not a code-category rule. Does the high-risk category language in review-assurance-floor-execution-plan.md mean CHK-002 should independently require 3x2 (or an explicit degraded-single-host fallback) at DONE regardless of REVIEW finding count, or does the finding-count threshold fully supersede/implement that categorical language for process-fact work? None of this story's PLAN artifacts mention review-escalation requirements or degraded-fallback eligibility.
